article_or_section: Understanding Georgia tax provisions; Power of Attorney
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base: 'Effective January 1, 2013, the taxable wage base in Georgia is 9,500 in accordance with 2012 Georgia House Bill 347'; employer pays UI tax on the first 9,500 of each employee's gross wages. New employer rate 2.7%, not reduced below 2.7% until 36 consecutive months of charges; UI taxes are employer-paid and cannot be deducted from employee wages (no employee contribution). Separate administrative assessment on taxable wages. POA: employer may appoint an agent by the GDOL Power of Attorney form mailed to the Adjudication Unit. The string 8,500 does not occur anywhere in the 164-page handbook, so the 8,500 in the FAQ answer (US-GA-002) is stale. Handbook is stated on the GDOL page to be under revision; 2026 rate notice with the new-employer rate not read.

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer Withholding Tax Guide 2026 (revised September 2026) - topic search
figure_or_rule_carried: Full-text search of the 54-page guide: nonresidents taxable for services in Georgia must be withheld; residents not withheld when services are outside Georgia and the other state requires withholding; bonuses withheld at the applicable rate (5.19% before the rate-change date, 4.99% after, see US-GA-001). Zero occurrences of: reciprocity, rounding, pay stub/pay statement; the only 'city' hits are addresses. No local income tax is described. Power of attorney/third-party authorization not in the guide.

figure_or_rule_carried: RD-1061 Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative (via Georgia Tax Center); RD-1062 one-time disclosure; RD-1063 Reporting Agent Authorization lets a business designate a company to sign and file returns and make deposits/payments (authority extends to the agent's employees); IRS Form 2848 accepted in lieu of Georgia form.
